decisions.reason: This drain housing builds directly on the firm's established drainage engineering and compatible system knowledge, so management would expect strong learning and improvement potential.
A floor-level shower drainage system sits at the center of the firm's current market direction, making it highly related to existing know-how and commercially important to retain.
Although more design-led, this shower drainage product still uses the firm's core technical and installation capabilities, so it is likely to be refined rather than withdrawn.
The integrated-slope shower element is somewhat broader than a pure drain component but remains close enough to the firm's installation expertise to justify continued development.
The backflow-protected basement floor drain is a technically specific extension of the firm's drainage competence and solves a clear building problem, which supports keeping it on the market.

The air-admittance valve is more peripheral to the firm's core drainage specialism, but it is still adjacent enough to plumbing system knowledge that management would more likely keep and test it than drop it immediately.
